paragraphs.text: A [ripe pu’er](shou:definition) from Yunnan, left to age as loose leaf rather than pressed into a cake or brick. Before that, the leaf went through the [wet pile](shou:wet-piling). Sun-dried leaf is wetted and heaped so that heat, moisture and microbes can work on it, and the pile is turned for a month or two before the leaf is dried. Yunnan’s state factories brought the method into production in 1973.
Ripe tea is ready to drink soon after it is made, so the years this lot has spent loose are time on top of that, not a wait it needed.

brewing.text: Use boiling water, about 7 grams to 100 ml, one quick rinse, then short steeps that lengthen as the leaf opens. Loose leaf needs no pick, and ripe tea forgives a heavy hand. Expect eight or more good cups.

notice.text: A smooth, sweet cup with earthy or woody notes, and in younger ripe tea a faint smell of the pile that fades with airing or in the first steeps.
